body: Hi @LefanTan, thanks for raising this issue and providing a CodeSandbox for it ! Indeed this is something we have overlooked, `Configure` does not persist in the URL. However calling `setUiState` without it doesn't seem to override the `SearchParameters` so it doesn't trigger any new network request nor a re-render. What's causing the re-render is actually the push action with the Next.js router, here's a screenshot of React DevTools profiler on the CodeSandbox you sent : There are 5 renders when clicking on a refinement list item : 1. Upon clicking on the refinement list item, it is re-rendered to show that it's checked 2. After receiving results from Algolia, we update the UI accordingly 3. Seems to be re-rendering Next.js links before the route push ? 4. Route has changed, `hydrateRoot` is called and re-renders the whole page 5. `RouteAnnouncer` gets re-rerendered That's 2 renders by InstantSearch, which is normal, and 3 by Next.js router. You can notice that even if `setUiState` is called twice, it actually doesn't trigger a render the second time, it's the Next router that does. This is more of a drawback from having to use Next.js router in order to have functioning `popState` actions. I think there are ways to push Next.js compatible state without triggering a re-render of the whole page, but I wouldn't recommend it as it's not future-proof. I think the second render (4th one actually) is fine as it's done in a debounced manner after the user has totally typed their query, and it's done when they would normally look at the results. Now I'm aware this creates unnecessary noise when using a custom `onStateChange`, so I'll still look for a fix for that (I think if we call `setUiState` only when the push wasn't from InstantSearch should do the trick), but be aware that this won't change the fact that a whole re-render is done when the URL changes.
